maya: quick heads-up — noticed a 25-40% regression in TTFT for long-context (32k) runs after landing the FP8 calibration path. repro on dedicated cluster A.
jon: ouch. can you paste the exact config you used? batch size, seq len, quant profile?
maya: batch=1, prefill seq=32k, decode max_new_tokens=512, kernel=fp8-mixed, calib=per-layer-ema, dynamic-batching=off
liam: did the runtime fall back to fp32 kernels anywhere? that usually kills TTFT if attention path reverts.
maya: good point — profiler shows fallback on some multihead matmuls. snippet: ```FALLBACK attention_matmul layer_22 -> fp32 (reason: zero-point mismatch)```
perf-bot: summary: prefill phase dominated by attention GEMM; prefill TTFT from 1800ms -> 2400ms after calib. decode TPS mostly unchanged at ~750 tok/s.
alice: that pattern indicates calibration added extra memcpy + dequant per-layer during prefill. decode reuses KV cache so overhead amortized.
sara: worth checking KV cache layout changes — did calib change KV dtype or stride? small stride differences can break our fused attention kernels.
maya: yes, calib added dtype=4bit-pole fallback for some heads, KV buffer layout switched from contiguous to interleaved for those layers.
liam: interleaved layout + mixed kernels = kernel selector picked a slower generic kernel for prefill because it preferred coalesced layout. decode uses cached packed KVs and hits optimized decode kernel, so TTFT regresses but TPS ok.
jon: can we force select the decode-optimized kernel for prefill too? maybe via heuristic: if seq_len>8k prefer decode kernel if it supports longer prefill?
alice: that would help TTFT but risk higher memory or slightly worse TPS in synthetic microbenchmarks. need perf numbers.
maya: ran a micro-bench: forcing decode kernel for prefill recovered TTFT to 1900ms, TPS dropped 5% in long-batch synthetic.
devops: note: forcing decode kernel increases peak GPU memory by ~400MB on A100-80G, might push some dedicated pools past limit.
sara: alternative: change batching heuristic — enable prefix-aggregation for small concurrent prefill requests to amortize dequant cost without switching kernels.
liam: also we could modify calibration step: prefer calibration profiles that keep KV layout contiguous even if slightly worse quant error. tradeoff quality vs TTFT.
maya: can we get an eval run on the quality set for the contig vs interleaved calib profiles? need to know BLEU/ROUGE delta.
jon: I'll run evals overnight. reward: if contig profile delta <0.3% we'll default to it for production.
perf-bot: queued job 2026-06-24-09: eval-contig-vs-interleaved (ETA 8h).
alice: additional quick fix: in kernel selector add a special-case: for prefill with seq_len>16k and on-device mem>threshold prefer packed-KV decode kernel if available. less risky than global forcing.
maya: sounds good. I'll prototype kernel-selector tweak and a small KV-layout compatibility shim. dropping logs + perf numbers here after prototype. thanks all :thumbsup:
